meta.titre: League of Nations Structures: the Assembly, the ILO and the commissions at work
meta.sous_theme: Structures and activities of the League of Nations
tags: league of nations organs and agencies

sections.contenu_markdown: Between 1922 and 1946 the territory we now call Cameroon was ruled as a League of Nations mandate, divided between Britain and France. The League that gave those mandates sat in Geneva, far from Douala or Buea, yet its decisions touched the lives of our grandparents. Examiners like to ask what the League's separate bodies actually did, because a candidate who only says that it "kept peace" has not answered. This course gives you the structures, their activities and a way to write short historical notes that earn full marks.

items: The First World War ended in 1918 and the Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919.
A member state is a country that has joined an international organisation.
A mandate was a territory taken from a defeated power after the war and placed under the supervision of the League.

sections.titre: What each League structure did and why it mattered
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Aims and headquarters

The League of Nations began work in 1920 and had its headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland. Its Covenant was part of the Treaty of Versailles. Its aims were to keep peace by collective security, to reduce armaments, to settle disputes by discussion and to improve living and working conditions. The United States never joined, because the American Senate refused to accept the treaty.

### The main structures and their activities

| Structure | What it was | Main activities |
|---|---|---|
| Assembly | Meeting of all member states, each with one vote | Debated world problems, admitted new members, chose the non-permanent members of the Council |
| Council | Smaller body with permanent and non-permanent members | Dealt with disputes and crises between states |
| ILO (International Labour Organisation) | Governments, employers and workers meeting together | Drew up international standards on working hours and conditions of work |
| Mandates Commission | Group of experts | Studied the yearly reports of Britain, France and other ruling powers on their mandates and received petitions from inhabitants; it could advise but not force |
| Health Organisation | Specialist body | Shared information and fought the spread of epidemic diseases |
| Refugee work | High Commissioner for Refugees, the Norwegian Fridtjof Nansen | Helped refugees and prisoners of war to return home or settle; the Nansen passport gave papers to stateless people |
| Disarmament Commission | Body preparing arms reduction | Worked towards smaller armies; the Disarmament Conference opened in Geneva in 1932 and ended without agreement |
| Permanent Court of International Justice | Court at The Hague | Gave judgements on legal disputes between states |

### Importance and weakness

The League settled some quarrels, for example the dispute over the Aaland Islands between Sweden and Finland, and the ILO still exists today. Yet the League had no army, decisions in the Assembly needed general agreement, and it failed to stop Japan in Manchuria in 1931 and Italy in Abyssinia in 1935.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to write notes on the activities of a named structure
variantes.contenu_markdown: Use a fixed pattern for each structure: one sentence saying what it was, then two or three separate activities, then one sentence on its importance or limits. Write only on the number of structures chosen. Name the structure exactly and keep to activities when the question says activities.

variantes.nom: Assess how successful the League was
variantes.quand_utiliser: When the command word is Assess, Discuss or To what extent
variantes.contenu_markdown: Give a balanced answer. Successes: the ILO, the Aaland Islands, the work for refugees and health. Failures: Manchuria, Abyssinia, the collapse of the disarmament talks, the absence of the United States and the lack of an army. End with a judgement such as: successful in social work, weak when great powers defied it.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the question mentions mandates or Cameroon
variantes.contenu_markdown: Germany lost Kamerun after 1918. In 1922 the League confirmed British and French mandates over the two parts. The Mandates Commission examined their reports. Do not confuse the League mandate (1922) with the United Nations trusteeship (1946).

sections.enonce_markdown: Explain how the League of Nations tried to improve the conditions of ordinary people between the two world wars. [8 marks]

etapes.action: Underline the command word and the key phrase.
etapes.justification: "Explain" needs reasons and details. "Conditions of ordinary people" points to social work, not to disputes between states.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Choose bodies that dealt with workers, health and refugees.

etapes.justification: A plan keeps each structure separate and prevents a list of names.
Say what it did and what that changed.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Governments, employers and workers met to agree standards on hours and conditions of work, so workers in many countries were protected.

etapes.justification: Give one concrete activity for each body.
etapes.resultat_markdown: The Health Organisation shared information to fight epidemics. Nansen, as High Commissioner, helped refugees and prisoners of war to return home, and the Nansen passport gave stateless people papers.

etapes.justification: A short judgement shows that you weighed the results even if the question does not say so.
etapes.resultat_markdown: These efforts helped many people, although the League could only advise and had no power to force states.

sections.conclusion_markdown: Model answer: The League tried to improve ordinary lives through its specialised bodies. The ILO brought governments, employers and workers together to agree international standards on hours and conditions of work. The Health Organisation shared information and worked against epidemic diseases. The High Commissioner for Refugees, Fridtjof Nansen, helped refugees and prisoners of war to return home, and the Nansen passport gave stateless people papers. These efforts improved many lives, although the League had to rely on the cooperation of its members.

items.erreur_markdown: The League of Nations was replaced by the United Nations in 1920.
items.pourquoi_faux: The League began in 1920 and the United Nations followed after the Second World War.
items.correction_markdown: The League worked from 1920 and the United Nations replaced it after 1945.

items.erreur_markdown: The League had its own army to punish aggressors.
items.pourquoi_faux: It had no army and depended on members to apply pressure.
items.correction_markdown: Say that it relied on persuasion and on measures taken by member states, and that this weakness hurt it in the 1930s.

items.erreur_markdown: The Assembly was the small body with permanent members.
items.pourquoi_faux: That describes the Council. The Assembly included all members, each with one vote.
items.correction_markdown: Assembly: all members. Council: smaller body with permanent and non-permanent members.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing "The ILO was a body of the League" and stopping there.
items.pourquoi_faux: The question asks for activities, so naming the body earns almost nothing.
items.correction_markdown: Add what it did: it set standards for hours and conditions of work and brought governments, employers and workers together.

items.erreur_markdown: The United States was a leading member of the League.
items.pourquoi_faux: The American Senate rejected the Versailles treaty and the United States never joined.
items.correction_markdown: Write that the absence of the United States weakened the League.

items.enonce_markdown: State the city where the League of Nations had its headquarters and give two aims of the League.
items.solution_markdown: Award a mark for each point. **Geneva.** Two aims from: to keep peace, to reduce armaments, to settle disputes peacefully, to improve living and working conditions.

items.enonce_markdown: Give two differences between the Assembly and the Council of the League of Nations.
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for any two clear differences. The Assembly included all member states with one vote each, while the Council was smaller. The Assembly met to debate world problems and to admit members, while the Council dealt with disputes and crises. **The Council contained permanent members, the Assembly did not.**

items.enonce_markdown: To what extent was the League of Nations successful between 1920 and 1939? [10 marks]
items.solution_markdown: Award marks for balance. Successes: the ILO set standards for workers, the Aaland Islands dispute was settled, refugees and health were helped. Failures: no army, the United States did not join, Japan in Manchuria (1931) and Italy in Abyssinia (1935) went unchecked, the Disarmament Conference failed. **Judgement: successful in social and humanitarian work, weak when great powers defied it.**

items_markdown: The League began in 1920 with headquarters in Geneva; its Covenant formed part of the Treaty of Versailles.
Assembly: all members, one vote each. Council: smaller, with permanent and non-permanent members.

Know one or two activities for each body: ILO (labour standards), Mandates Commission (supervised reports), Health Organisation (fight epidemics), Refugee work (Nansen), Disarmament Commission (arms talks of 1932).
Cameroon was a League mandate from 1922; the UN trusteeship started in 1946.
In notes questions give what it was, separate activities, then importance.
Weaknesses: no army, United States absent, failures in Manchuria and Abyssinia.
